name: Nimzo-Indian, Queen's Indian & Catalan
summary: Aron Nimzowitsch's revolutionary hypermodern masterpiece. Black controls the e4 square from afar with ...Bb4 and ...b6/Bb7, willingly giving up the bishop pair to inflict doubled c-pawns on White.
keyConcepts: Control of e4 from a distance

subVariations.name: Nimzo-Indian: Rubinstein Variation (4.e3)
subVariations.description: Akiba Rubinstein's classical system. White accepts doubled c-pawns in exchange for the bishop pair and a solid pawn center.
subVariations.whitePlan: Utilize bishop pair on c4/d3, prepare e4 central breakthrough.
subVariations.blackPlan: Lock the center with ...c5 and ...dxc4, target the doubled c3/c4 pawns.

subVariations.name: Nimzo-Indian: Classical / Capablanca (4.Qc2)
subVariations.description: José Raúl Capablanca's system: 4.Qc2 avoids doubled c-pawns by recapturing with the queen, keeping a pristine pawn structure.
subVariations.whitePlan: Build broad center with f3/e4, utilize spatial superiority.
subVariations.blackPlan: Fianchetto bishop on b7, break with ...d5, pressure e4 square.

subVariations.name: Nimzo-Indian: Sämisch Variation (4.a3)
subVariations.description: Fritz Sämisch's aggressive system: White forces 4.a3 immediately, welcoming doubled pawns for direct kingside attacking chances with f3/e4.
subVariations.whitePlan: Build pawn center with f3/e4, attack down the g-file and kingside.
subVariations.blackPlan: Blockade c4 pawn with ...Nd7/Na5, pressure White's queenside weaknesses.

subVariations.name: Nimzo-Indian: 4.f3 System (Shirov Attack)
subVariations.description: Alexei Shirov's attacking system: White plays 4.f3 to build an immediate e4/d4 steamroller in the center.
subVariations.whitePlan: Advance d5 and e4, utilize bishop pair, launch kingside assault.
subVariations.blackPlan: Counterstrike with 5...e5!, exploit light-squared diagonals with ...Bc5.

subVariations.name: Nimzo-Indian: Leningrad Variation (4.Bg5)
subVariations.description: White pins the knight with 4.Bg5, leading to Benoni-like closed pawn chains after ...c5 and d5.
subVariations.whitePlan: Maintain Bg5 pin, attack with f4 on kingside.
subVariations.blackPlan: Lock the center with ...e5, unpin with ...Qe7, attack doubled c-pawns.

subVariations.name: Nimzo-Indian: Hübner Variation (4.e3 c5 5.Bd3 Nc6)
subVariations.description: Robert Hübner's closed positional system: Black locks the center with ...e5 and targets White's immobile c4 pawn with ...Ne7-g6.
subVariations.whitePlan: Break open the kingside with f4, utilize bishop pair.
subVariations.blackPlan: Lock the center completely, maneuver knight to g6, blockade light squares.

subVariations.name: Nimzo-Indian: Romanishin / 4.g3 System
subVariations.description: Oleg Romanishin's hybrid system combining Nimzo-Indian piece pin with a Catalan fianchetto on g2.
subVariations.whitePlan: Control long diagonal with Bg2, use queen on c3 to pressure e5.
subVariations.blackPlan: Advance d4 pawn wedge, utilize central space advantage, coordinate pieces.

subVariations.name: Queen's Indian: Classical 4.g3 Ba6 Line
subVariations.description: The hypermodern masterpiece of the Queen's Indian. Black develops the bishop to a6 to attack c4, provoking 5.b3 before regrouping to e7.
subVariations.whitePlan: Occupy e5 outpost with Ne5, prepare e4 central expansion.
subVariations.blackPlan: Fortify d5 with ...c6, challenge e5 knight, counterstrike in the center.

subVariations.name: Queen's Indian: Classical 4.g3 Bb7 Line
subVariations.description: Classical central battle on the long diagonal. Black anchors the knight on e4 and supports it with ...f5 (Dutch formation).
subVariations.whitePlan: Break open the center with d5, undermine Black's e4 knight outpost.
subVariations.blackPlan: Reinforce e4 with ...f5, activate pieces on f6 and a6, maintain dark-square grip.

subVariations.name: Queen's Indian: 4.e3 System (Rubinstein)
subVariations.description: Quiet, super-solid positional line avoiding the fianchetto and playing for a classical IQP or Colle-like setup.
subVariations.whitePlan: Develop bishops on d3/b2, prepare central e4 push with Qe2.
subVariations.blackPlan: Anchor knight on e4, coordinate pieces on d7/d6, counterstrike in the center.

subVariations.name: Queen's Indian: Petrosian System (4.a3)
subVariations.description: Tigran Petrosian's system: 4.a3 prevents ...Bb4 and allows White to build an uncontested broad pawn center with e4.
subVariations.whitePlan: Build broad d4/e4 pawn center, use active bishop on d3 to attack kingside.
subVariations.blackPlan: Undermine White's center with ...c5, pressure d4 pawn, utilize b7 bishop.

subVariations.name: Queen's Indian: Miles System (4.Bf4)
subVariations.description: Tony Miles's active development of the dark bishop to f4 before e3, controlling key diagonals.
subVariations.whitePlan: Control e5 square with Bf4, maintain solid center with e3, push d5.
subVariations.blackPlan: Centralize queen on d5, strike with ...c5, utilize the b7 bishop.

subVariations.name: Bogo-Indian Defense: 4.Bd2 Line
subVariations.description: Efim Bogoljubow's defense: Black checks on b4 and defends the bishop with ...Qe7, aiming to trade light bishops.
subVariations.whitePlan: Control long diagonal with Bg2/Bc3, push d5 to claim space.
subVariations.blackPlan: Trade light bishops, anchor knight on e4, reroute knight via Nb8-d7.

subVariations.name: Bogo-Indian Defense: 4.Nbd2 Line
subVariations.description: White blocks the check with the knight on d2, retaining the bishop pair after 5.a3 Bxd2+.
subVariations.whitePlan: Utilize bishop pair, expand on queenside with b4, control central files.
subVariations.blackPlan: Fianchetto bishop on b7, anchor knight on e4, counterattack centrally.

subVariations.name: Catalan Opening: Open Classical (6...dxc4 7.Qc2)
subVariations.description: Vladimir Kramnik's supreme theoretical weapon. Black grabs the c4 pawn and counterstrikes with ...e5, while White dominates the long diagonal.
subVariations.whitePlan: Exploit powerful g2 bishop and Black's doubled c-pawns, win back c4.
subVariations.blackPlan: Activate pieces with ...Ng4 and ...Be6, counterattack down open b-file.

subVariations.name: Catalan Opening: Closed System (6...Nbd7)
subVariations.description: Black maintains a solid pawn fortress with ...c6 and ...Nbd7, allowing White to expand centrally with e4-e5.
subVariations.whitePlan: Advance e4-e5, establish kingside spatial advantage, attack Black's knight.
subVariations.blackPlan: Fianchetto bishop on b7, maneuver knight to e8/c7, counterattack along c-file.

subVariations.name: Catalan Opening: Modern 7.Qc2 a6
subVariations.description: Black plays 8...Bd7 and 9...Bc6 to neutralize White's monster g2 bishop on the long diagonal.
subVariations.whitePlan: Pin with Bg5, maintain queen on c2/d1, push e4 to seize center.
subVariations.blackPlan: Occupy long diagonal with ...Bc6/Be4, achieve harmonious piece equality.

subVariations.name: Catalan Opening: 4...Bb4+ Variation
subVariations.description: Black delivers an immediate check with ...Bb4+ to disrupt White's setup before retreating to e7.
subVariations.whitePlan: Develop solidly with Bf4 and Rd1, prepare e4 central breakthrough.
subVariations.blackPlan: Build solid c6/d5 base, fianchetto on b7, coordinate smoothly.

subVariations.name: Neo-Catalan Defense (1.d4 Nf6 2.c4 e6 3.Nf3 d5 4.g3)
subVariations.description: Black defends the extra c4 pawn with ...a5 and ...b5, leading to queenside structural battles.
subVariations.whitePlan: Puncture Black's pawn chain with a4 and b3, exploit the g2 bishop.
subVariations.blackPlan: Hold onto queenside material, develop bishop to b7, defend c6.

subVariations.name: Blumenfeld Countergambit (3.Nf3 c5 4.d5 b5)
subVariations.description: High-voltage countergambit with 4...b5! Black seizes the bishop pair and creates a powerful queen on f6.
subVariations.whitePlan: Use Nb5 outpost and d6 wedge, attack Black's uncastled king.
subVariations.blackPlan: Use queen on f6, push central pawns, coordinate bishop pair on b7.
